'''Sir David Jack''' (22 February 1924 – 8 November 2011<ref name=tg>{{cite news|title=Sir David Jack|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/finance-obituaries/8897458/Sir-David-Jack.html|accessdate=25 November 2011|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=17 November 2011}}</ref><ref name=herald>{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/mobile/comment/obituaries/sir-david-jack-1.1135726|newspaper=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|date=19 November 2011|title=Sir David Jack}}</ref>) was a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[pharmacologist]] and [[medicinal chemist]] who specialised in the development of drugs for treating [[asthma]]. He was head of research and development at [[Glaxo]] from 1978 until 1987.

==Early life and education==

Jack was born the sixth and youngest child of a coal miner, in [[Markinch]], [[Fife]], [[Scotland]].<ref name="Timesobit">{{cite web
| url         = https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/uk-travel/scotland-travel/sir-david-jack-b7lmgj53966
| title       = Obituary, Sir David Jack
| work   = [[The Times]]
| date = 18 November 2011
| access-date  = 18 November 2011
}}</ref>  He attended [[Buckhaven High School]] before turning down a place at [[Edinburgh University]] to become an apprentice [[pharmacist]]. In 1944, having completed his apprenticeship, he began a BSc course in chemistry and pharmacy at the [[Royal Technical College]], [[Glasgow]].  He won a number of undergraduate prizes and graduated with first class honours.<ref name="Timesobit"/>

==Career==

He turned down an offer to study for a doctorate and instead worked as an assistant lecturer at the [[University of Glasgow]].<ref name="frs"/><ref name="Timesobit"/>

In 1951 he joined the pharmaceutical company [[Glaxo Laboratories]], moving to Smith Kline and French in 1953.<ref name="Timesobit"/> In 1961 he became director of research at [[Allen and Hanburys]], a subsidiary of Glaxo, and served as Glaxo's research and development director from 1978 until his official retirement in 1987.<ref name=tg/>

Jack was known for heading a research team which developed the following drugs:

* [[Beclometasone]] in 1962
* [[Salbutamol]] or Albuterol in 1966, 
* [[Ranitidine]] in 1977,
* [[Sumatriptan]] in 1984,
* [[Salmeterol]] or serevent in 1985,
* [[Ondansetron]] in 1987,
* and [[Fluticasone propionate]] in 1993.

==Honours==

Jack was appointed a Commander of the [[Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[1982 Birthday Honours]],<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=49008|page=8|date=11 June 1982|supp=y}}</ref> and knighted for services to the pharmaceutical industry in 1993.<ref name="Timesobit"/>

In 1987, he was awarded an Honorary Degree (Doctor of Science) by the [[University of Bath]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bath.ac.uk/ceremonies/hongrads/ |title=Honorary Graduates 1989 to present |publisher=[[University of Bath]] |work=bath.ac.uk |accessdate=18 February 2012 |archive-date=19 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151219000643/http://www.bath.ac.uk/ceremonies/hongrads/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
